head: 6ca4032b5073dab18dcaabb5e04dac67c7b3f54e
scope: Complete two-file upper delta; lower API was independently reviewed at parent. Consumer cache/error/worker semantics plus retained actual-module typing and selected native proof. Not a whole Native stack/current-runtime verdict.

source_review.detail: The old consumer already decoded its first repaired AST rather than reparsing bytes. Old encoder sanitized that same AST again. New API returns the single repaired writer-input AST, which state_of_yojson consumes inside the same submit_cpu_or_inline callback. Safe_ops repair is idempotent on repaired UTF8/control bytes; numeric variants/order/duplicates are unchanged. Thus the lower API writer-AST versus wire-parsed-AST distinction does not introduce a new consumer semantic change here.

Encoding error still maps to Persistence_failed with the same ledger encoding prefix, skips state_of_yojson on writer failure, and exits before primary write/cache publication. Actual domain decode remains a Result beside encoded content; no fallback/default authorizes a bad state.

Unchanged write order: primary commit first, cache keep only on successful FileSystem commit with no mirror error plus successful domain decode, all other cases forget. Memory backend remains authority over local mirror and successful backend commit with mirror warning stays success; recovery-mirror failure remains warning after primary success. No new cache authority, fallback promotion, IO or ACK was added.

Serialization, one sanitizer traversal and state_of_yojson stay in the same CPU-pool job. Only content and typed domain-decode result cross back to caller. Returned raw AST is not newly cached; only the same decoded state may enter the existing File_version_cache after commit. No new global index/lazy value/promise/mutable retention or cross-worker authority is introduced.

Unix.lstat and directory recursion stay identical. The previous non-directory wildcard is replaced with all six current non-directory Unix.file_kind constructors; S_LNK is still unlinked instead of followed. Existing missing-path handling and cleanup exception policy are unchanged. This closes fatal warning4 without adding source/control heuristics.

recorded_native_results.whole_test_failure: Pre-existing fragile matches over closed Schedule store_error fail fatal warning4; full suite did not link or run.
recorded_native_results.prior_selected_r1_failure: Actual TestDeps referenced missing masc_test_unsetenv at link; retained r1 error. r2 compiled unchanged maintained test_env_stubs.c and linked the same actual consumer/selection, with no dummy symbol/interface.
recorded_native_results.scope: Recorded complete Schedule MLI/ML and complete TestDeps typecheck plus exact selected cases using compatible prebuilt dependencies and renamed lower/consumer units. Reviewer verified source/hash/flags/logs but did not rerun compiler, linker or tests. Full Test suite remains unexecuted.

limits: No reviewer native/Dune/CI/test execution, GitHub query/write, runtime API, restart/install, Git/ref/index or product source mutation. Only private review evidence written.

Selected runner verifies ten concrete behaviors: observer after unlock/no-op silence, Memory backend/mirror authority, recovery mirror failure, parseable last-good, CPU-pool write/miss read, unchanged-file/written-state cache and repaired-state parity. It does not establish full Schedule regression success.
No server CPU/RSS, fleet, provider, installed-binary or current runtime recovery measurement. Removing one duplicate traversal is a source-level fact, not a whole-server timing claim.
No prior-art API or arbitrary wire parsing equivalence claimed; this consumer already decoded writer-input AST before the change.
